answer: Each identity registers one haven echo station: a post, a horizon marker, and a 75-credit bond. Each epoch it files ping time, return time, temperature, and serial. An auditor recomputes range with the public echo-speed table and checks the horizon angle. An error over 2 percent, a reused ping, or one post for two identities burns the bond. The first filing costs 39; the kth costs 39+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7032 and 1000 fakes cost 3,535,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented sounder fails because serial and angle bind one log to one station. An honest agent pays 39 once and recovers its bond.
